clue.text: Agenda is to get Times, say, regularly

definitions.meaning: the printed list of business for a sitting of Parliament or a meeting
to arrange with a newsagent for a daily newspaper such as The Times to be delivered

explanation.surface: Someone's plan for the day is simply to pick up the newspaper as usual.
explanation.definitionFit: The official programme of business for a parliamentary session is a printed agenda, so the two are synonyms.

clue.text: Protection for walls of crude shed

parts.note: crude means rough, unrefined
a snake casts, or sheds, its skin

explanation.surface: A rough-and-ready garden shed needs something to protect its walls.
explanation.definitionFit: Coarse plaster of lime and gravel is thrown onto exterior walls as a weatherproof coating.

clue.text: Pretended madman clad in ragged garb

indicators.note: the name is dressed in, so sits inside, the run of letters across these two words

explanation.surface: A man feigning insanity goes about in tattered clothes.
explanation.walkthrough: In King Lear, Gloucester's son disguises himself as the mad beggar Poor Tom.
explanation.definitionFit: Shakespeare's character in King Lear feigns lunacy as Poor Tom to escape his pursuers.

clue.text: Writer getting nothing out of job, initially?

definitions.text: Writer getting nothing out of job, initially?

parts.words: Writer getting nothing out of job, initially?
parts.note: take the nothing, O, out of the word job and you have the initials J B, those of a famous English novelist and playwright

explanation.surface: An author earns nothing at all from his first piece of work.
explanation.walkthrough: J. B. Priestley wrote An Inspector Calls; 'initially' points to his initials rather than to first letters.
explanation.definitionFit: J. B. Priestley was an English novelist and dramatist, so he is a writer whose initials match the trimmed word.

clue.text: Crude heavy metal is unpleasant thing at club

parts.note: a pig of a job is a nasty, awkward one
an iron is a type of golf club

explanation.surface: Loud heavy metal music is a nuisance to hear at a nightclub.
explanation.definitionFit: Iron straight from the blast furnace, before refining, is cast in rough bars and is the crude form of that metal.

clue.text: One took a bow, having distributed cold beer

indicators.note: the letters of the beer are dealt out and set down in a new order

parts.note: C is the abbreviation for cold, as on a tap

explanation.surface: A performer took a bow after handing round chilled beer.
explanation.walkthrough: A rebec is a medieval bowed instrument; the surface's performer taking a bow is the misdirection.
explanation.definitionFit: A medieval stringed instrument was played with a bow, so it is one that took a bow, in the past tense.

clue.text: Division of European capital is a nuisance

definitions.meaning: Budapest was formed by uniting Buda on one bank of the Danube with ... on the other

explanation.surface: One district of a European city has become an irritation.
explanation.definitionFit: Something irritating that bothers you, like a fly or a whining child, is a nuisance.

clue.text: Confine ambitious type as clerical worker

parts.note: to pen animals is to confine them
a pusher is someone forceful and ambitious

explanation.surface: An overly ambitious employee is kept in a back office as a clerk.
explanation.definitionFit: A derogatory term for an office clerk who shuffles paper all day.

clue.text: Military HQ, such as Pentagon

definitions.meaning: Supreme Headquarters Allied Powers Europe, NATO's command centre
a pentagon is an example of a geometric figure

explanation.surface: The Pentagon is the classic example of a military headquarters.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads Pentagon as the US defence building; here it is the five-sided figure.
explanation.definitionFit: A pentagon is a geometric figure, and NATO's European headquarters bears this acronym.

clue.text: Blowing one's trumpet, but hiding name — such incompetence

indicators.note: the trumpeting word conceals, so holds within it, the abbreviation that follows

parts.note: bugling is sounding a bugle, a kind of trumpet

explanation.surface: Someone boasts about themselves while keeping their own name quiet, a sign of real ineptitude.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Blowing one's trumpet' suggests boasting, but here it is literal.
explanation.definitionFit: Clumsy mishandling of a task is gross ineptitude, the noun sense here.

clue.text: Cocky little type, weighing less than a feather?"

definitions.meaning: a small breed of domestic fowl, the cock noted for being aggressive
in boxing the weight class just below featherweight

explanation.surface: A conceited little chap is so slight he weighs less than a feather.
explanation.definitionFit: A miniature chicken breed, and the boxing division lighter than featherweight, share this name.

clue.text: Refrain from beginning to criticise old god

indicators.note: only the opening letter of the word criticise is wanted

parts.note: Horus was the falcon-headed god of ancient Egypt

explanation.surface: Avoid starting to find fault with an ancient deity.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Refrain' looks like a verb meaning hold back; it is the noun, a repeated part of a song.
explanation.definitionFit: The repeated section of a song sung after each verse is a refrain.

clue.text: Got money back, as car comes in bright colour

indicators.note: the car's word enters the colour's word and sits within it

parts.note: red is a bright colour
a coupe is a two-door car

explanation.surface: Someone recovered their costs because the bright red car they bought went up in value.
explanation.definitionFit: To recoup is to recover money spent or lost, so this is a past-tense synonym.

clue.text: Stroke part of eye

definitions.meaning: a single blow with a whip
one of the hairs fringing the eyelid

explanation.surface: A blow to the eye area.
explanation.definitionFit: A whip's stroke is a blow, and an eyelash is a hair on the lid.

clue.text: Running around set of seedlings, working in field

indicators.note: the running word is placed around the line of seedlings

parts.note: haring is running fast, like a hare
seedlings are planted in a row

explanation.surface: A gardener rushes round a row of young plants while working outdoors.
explanation.definitionFit: Breaking up soil with a toothed farm implement is a kind of work done in a field.

clue.text: Part of country where I crash convertible in narrow road

indicators.note: the shuffled letters go inside the road's word

parts.note: a lane is a narrow road

indicators.note: something convertible can be changed in form, so these letters can be rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A motorist describes the spot where they wrote off their convertible on a country lane.
explanation.walkthrough: 'convertible' looks like a car but is the anagram signal; the answer is a county in north-west England.
explanation.definitionFit: A county is a division of a country, and this is one in north-west England.

clue.text: Obsession with using colour originally in supplement

indicators.note: the letter is placed inside the supplement's word

parts.note: an addition is something supplementary

indicators.note: the first letter of the word colour is taken

explanation.surface: Someone is fixated on adding colour to things.
explanation.walkthrough: 'using' is drug slang for taking drugs, so 'Obsession with using' defines dependency.
explanation.definitionFit: A compulsive dependency on drugs is the state of being hooked on using them.

clue.text: Create-commotion, as Squeers was said regularly to do

indicators.note: the phrase spoken out loud matches a different spelling

parts.note: what Squeers regularly did was to lift his stick and beat pupils, to raise a cane

explanation.surface: Squeers was famous for causing an uproar.
explanation.walkthrough: Wackford Squeers is the brutal schoolmaster in Dickens's Nicholas Nickleby who regularly beat his boys. 'Raise cane' sounds like 'raise Cain'. The hyphen in the definition is a print slip.
explanation.definitionFit: To raise Cain is an idiom meaning to make a great fuss or uproar.

clue.text: Imbibing right whisky, remained naively optimistic

indicators.note: the remaining word drinks in, so holds within it, the following pieces

parts.note: stayed means remained
rye is a whisky made from rye grain

explanation.surface: Drinking the proper whisky, someone stayed dreamily hopeful.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone idealistic and unrealistically hopeful is described as having stars in their eyes.

clue.text: Year I had on course for language

parts.note: I had contracts to I'd
a dish is a course of a meal

explanation.surface: Someone recalls a year when they had a dish on a language course.
explanation.definitionFit: The Germanic tongue historically spoken by Ashkenazi Jews is a language.

clue.text: No honest man is rejected for the bar

indicators.note: being rejected means being turned back, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: a liar is no honest man

explanation.surface: A dishonest man is refused entry to the pub bar.
explanation.definitionFit: A rail is a horizontal rod, so it is a bar.

clue.text: Married love experienced, based on intuitive communication

indicators.note: the love and experience pieces are built on, so follow, the telepathy piece

parts.note: ESP is extrasensory perception
love is zero in tennis, O
used means experienced, as in used to hardship

explanation.surface: A couple wed after experiencing love that relied on an almost telepathic bond.
explanation.definitionFit: To espouse someone is an old word for to wed them, so this past form means wed.

clue.text: Powerful movement convinced government leader to join in'

indicators.note: the leading letter joins in, so goes inside, the word for convinced

parts.note: sure means convinced

indicators.note: the first letter of the word government is taken

explanation.surface: A political movement persuaded the head of government to take part.
explanation.walkthrough: The stray apostrophe after 'in' is a print slip.
explanation.definitionFit: A sudden powerful forward rush, as of a wave or crowd, is a surge.

clue.text: Title of book one has turned up

indicators.note: in a down entry, turning up means the letters are read from bottom to top

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: Someone has turned up the title of a book.
explanation.definitionFit: In colonial India this was a respectful form of address, a title like sir.

clue.text: Treat luxuriously prepared on holiday island

indicators.note: in an across entry, the second piece sits on, so after, the first

parts.note: Cos, or Kos, is a Greek holiday island
set means ready, prepared

explanation.surface: A treat laid on for guests on a Greek holiday island.
explanation.definitionFit: To cosset is to pamper someone, treating them with indulgent care.

clue.text: Son's desire to be smart

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for son
a wish is a desire

explanation.surface: A son wants to look stylish.
explanation.definitionFit: Swish is informal for fashionable or stylish, so it means smart.

clue.text: Spirit of anger overcoming one

indicators.note: the anger word comes over, so encloses, the numeral

parts.note: wrath is anger
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A spirit of anger overpowers someone.
explanation.definitionFit: A ghostly apparition is a spirit.

clue.text: Not liking to return skirt I consider short

indicators.note: returning means the word for skirt is read backwards

parts.note: a mini is a short skirt

indicators.note: short means the word loses its last letter

parts.note: to call something good is to consider it so

explanation.surface: Someone dislikes having to take back a skirt they think is too short.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to return' turns MINI into INIM; 'short' cuts CALL to CAL.
explanation.definitionFit: Inimical means hostile or unfriendly, so not liking someone.

clue.text: Composer looked up to by Boers

definitions.meaning: Afrikaans for mountain, something Boers would look up to

explanation.surface: A composer revered by Afrikaners.
explanation.walkthrough: 'looked up to' sounds like admiration but is literal: a mountain is something you look up at.
explanation.definitionFit: Alban Berg, composer of Wozzeck, and the Afrikaans word for mountain share this spelling.

clue.text: Cough here politely delayed

definitions.meaning: a polite person coughs with a hand over the mouth

explanation.surface: A polite cough held up proceedings.
explanation.definitionFit: Being late with payments or work means being in arrears or delayed.
